text:
elaine: FYI BlueHarvest reported repeated 429s starting ~2026-03-16 03:00 UTC, every top-of-minute for ~30s windows. They say it started after deploying a new batching client.
mike: do we have request ids or response headers? 429 sample would help (x-rate-limit, retry-after).
elaine: pasted customer snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 1200
 x-ratelimit-usage: 1223
retry-after: 1
x-request-id: rh-8f6a3c
```
elaine: they also sent this note: "we send 6 parallel streams, each issues bursts of 20 requests at minute boundary"
sam: that pattern screams minute-boundary synchronization + no jitter. Edge shows same x-api-key hitting short windows of high RPM then dropping. I see throttle logs: `throttle=window_limit:1200 used=1235 window_end=1679995200`
priya: can you repro locally? If it's parallel streams sending small batches at minute tick you'll see request amplification from retries.
mike: ask customer for a request log with timestamps (ms precision) for one spike. Also ask if they use exponential backoff; naive immediate retries amplify.
elaine: they attached timestamps (example): `03:00:00.100`, `03:00:00.120`, `03:00:00.140` across 6 clients. Lots of tight clustering.
sam: repro plan: run a small script that opens 6 connections and issues 20 requests at exactly second 0 of each minute. Use `hey` or `wrk` to simulate. Example: 
```
for i in 1..6; do (sleep $((RANDOM%2)); for j in 1..20; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"x"}' $API & done; wait) & done; wait
```
priya: note the `sleep $((RANDOM%2))` is minimal jitter; for minute-aligned bursts you need randomized offset > few seconds. Recommend customer: add randomized jitter up to 15s and a leaky-bucket token limiter on client side.
elaine: they asked if Redwood can change server-side smoothing.
sam: we already have prefix caching + automatic batching, but server-side can't fully absorb synchronous minute spikes if bucket is exhausted. Two options: 1) quota bump / Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, 2) client smoothing + retry jitter.
mike: also check if their requests are streaming vs discrete generations — streaming connections hold concurrency slots longer and increase concurrent token usage.
elaine: customer says they switched to streaming to reduce latency which increased in-flight request count.
sam: confirm: streaming per-connection concurrency counts toward TPM/RPM. When in-flight windows hit, edge sends 429s.
priya: quick mitigation we can recommend immediately: reduce parallel streams from 6 -> 2, add randomized jitter 0-15s, implement exponential backoff with full jitter on 429, and switch from synchronous retries to queued retry with cap of 2 in-flight retries per client.
mike: created internal ticket RH-4872 to consider temporary quota bump for BlueHarvest while they roll smoothing changes. If Sales approve, we can apply a short runway bump.
elaine: customer engineering asked for repro steps to test their client changes before rolling. Provide a minimal script: 
```
# simulate minute boundary burst with jitter
KEY=sk-redwood-test
API=https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
for t in 1..6; do (
  jitter=$((RANDOM % 15))
  sleep $jitter
  for i in 1..20; do
    curl -s -X POST $API -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
  done
  wait
) & done; wait
```
Run with/without jitter to compare. Watch x-ratelimit headers.
priya: also suggested adding token-bucket client-side pseudocode: `tokens = capacity; refill every 1s; if tokens>0 send else queue` — helps with minute spikes.
sam: from infra logs: 03:00:00 global windows reset and their burst crosses the per-key limiter leading to short 429 ramp. I recommend adding per-key smoothing on our side as a conservative measure but that requires product review.
mike: action items: (1) ask BlueHarvest to deploy jitter + cap streams and test with script; (2) ops to evaluate a 7-day quota bump and run cost estimate; (3) product to review server-side smoothing/ingress de-dup/queueing for predictable minute-boundary spikes.
elaine: I'll send the mitigation steps to customer and attach repro script. Also flagged for Sales contact.
infra-bot: ticket RH-4872 created and linked to customer id BH-978. SLA: P2.
priya: if customer wants immediate relief and has sensitive SLAs, advocate Dedicated capacity—predictable throughput avoids these minute-aligned amplification issues.
mike: keeping thread open until they confirm mitigation results. :thumbsup:
